**Avatar Stack.** Up to a few overlapping round avatars, then the group's size.

**When:** Who is in a group, in a card or a row (38 investors, 3 reviewers), when their names matter less than how many. For one person use `avatar`; for a list of people use `list` or `table`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `count` | the group's size, shown after them (default the number of people) |
| `most` | the most avatars drawn (default 3) |
| `people` | list of { name, src? }: the avatars drawn |
| `size` | avatar size: small (default) or normal |

**Styles:** `.avatar-stack` `.avatar-stack-count` `.avatar-stack-face` `.avatar-stack-faces`


#### `bar-chart`

**Bar Chart.** Vertical bars per bucket, stacked by series with toned colours, axis labels, an optional scale, and a legend.

**When:** Counts over time or per category: tokens per day, runs per hour, alerts per device, stacked by kind. For a tiny live trend in a status bar use `sparkline`; for one fraction use `meter`; for one headline number use `stat-tile`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `axis` | show the top value and 0 on the left |
| `bar` | bar width in pixels (default 18) |
| `buckets` | list of { label, values = { one number per series }, tooltip, dim (drawn faded: a period still running) } |
| `every` | label every Nth bucket (default 1) |
| `gap` | pixels between bucket slots (default 4) |
| `grid` | false hides the gridlines `ticks` draws |
| `grow` | the buckets share the width given instead of taking `slot` pixels each |
| `height` | plot height in pixels (default 120) |
| `legend` | false hides the legend |
| `max` | value at the top (default the largest stack) |
| `series` | list of { name, tone (accent\|success\|warning\|danger\|muted\|c1..c6), color (hex) }; bottom of the stack first |
| `slot` | pixels each bucket takes, bar plus room for its label (default 30) |
| `ticks` | steps on the scale: labels from 0 to `max` at each step, with dashed gridlines (implies `axis`) |
| `unit` | suffix for the scale, e.g. "k" or "%" |

**Styles:** `.bar-chart` `.bar-chart-accent` `.bar-chart-bar` `.bar-chart-c1` `.bar-chart-c2` `.bar-chart-c3` `.bar-chart-c4` `.bar-chart-c5` `.bar-chart-c6` `.bar-chart-danger` `.bar-chart-dim` `.bar-chart-empty` `.bar-chart-grid` `.bar-chart-key` `.bar-chart-label` `.bar-chart-legend` `.bar-chart-muted` `.bar-chart-plot` `.bar-chart-scale` `.bar-chart-success` `.bar-chart-swatch` `.bar-chart-warning`

```lua
local bar_chart = use "bar-chart"

bar_chart {
	axis = true, unit = "k", height = 120,
	series = { { name = "Input", tone = "c1" }, { name = "Output", tone = "c4" }, { name = "Cache", tone = "muted" } },
	buckets = {
		{ label = "Mon", values = { 42, 18, 12 } },
		{ label = "Tue", values = { 55, 22, 20 } },
		-- ...
	},
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/bar-chart.luau`.

#### `chat-message`

**Chat Message.** A chat message: the user's as a bubble on the right, the assistant's as text under an icon and a name, with anything else inside.

**When:** Each turn of a conversation with an agent or a person, stacked in a scrolling column over a `composer`. For a comment on a pull request use `comment-card`; for a notification use `toast`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | more after the text: a `thinking` fold, cards, lists |
| `author` | the assistant's name in its header; no header without it |
| `from` | "user" (a bubble on the right) or "assistant" (default) |
| `icon` | the icon in the header's chip (default sparkles) |
| `text` | the message's text; paragraphs split on blank lines |

**Styles:** `.chat-message` `.chat-message-author` `.chat-message-bubble` `.chat-message-chip` `.chat-message-head`

```lua
local chat_message = use "chat-message"
local thinking = use "thinking"

chat_message { from = "user", text = "Which deal should I look at first?" }

	author = "Sales agent", text = "Start with Lumen Retail: the biggest deal at risk.",
	thinking { seconds = 4, open = state.thought, msg = "toggle-thought" },
}
```

```lua
local code_view = use "code-view"

}
```

#### `dot-chart`

**Dot Chart.** Columns of rounded squares, one per bucket: filled for this period, pale up to the previous period's value; with an axis and labels.

**When:** A daily or weekly count compared with the period before (signups, orders), where the squares' rhythm reads better than smooth bars. For stacked counts by kind use `bar-chart`; for a balance against a floor use `forecast-chart`; for a trend line use `ui.line`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | this period's colour (default accent) |
| `columns` | list of { current, previous?, tooltip? }, left to right |
| `labels` | labels under the chart, spread evenly from the first column to the last |
| `max` | the value at the top |
| `rows` | squares in a full column (default 8): each is max / rows |
| `shade` | the previous period's colour (default muted-foreground at 12%) |
| `size` | a square's side in pixels (default 13) |
| `ticks` | axis labels from the top (max) down to 0, evenly spaced |

**Styles:** `.dot-chart` `.dot-chart-column` `.dot-chart-dot` `.dot-chart-label` `.dot-chart-tick`

```lua
local dot_chart = use "dot-chart"

dot_chart { columns = { { current = 48, previous = 60 }, { current = 70, previous = 61 }, { current = 55, previous = 66 }, { current = 90, previous = 85 }, { current = 82, previous = 74 }, { current = 104, previous = 118 } }, labels = { "Oct 2", "Oct 5", "Oct 8" }, max = 120, rows = 8, ticks = { "120", "60", "0" } }
```

| Prop | Meaning |

#### `forecast-chart`

**Forecast Chart.** Bars over periods with each change above them, a dashed floor with the held part hatched, the low period flagged, and a value axis.

**When:** A balance or capacity projected over weeks or months against a minimum (cash against a floor, stock against a reorder point). For counts per bucket, stacked by kind, use `bar-chart`; for a small trend use `sparkline` or `ui.line`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bar` | each bar's width in pixels (default 28) |
| `bars` | list of { label, value, delta? ("+9.2"), note? (text over the bar instead), current? (drawn dark), low? (flagged), tooltip? } |
| `event` | key of the message a bar sends: { [event] = index }; none without it |
| `floor` | a value drawn across, dashed; the part of each bar under it is hatched |
| `height` | the plot's height in pixels (default 260) |
| `max` | the value at the top of the plot |
| `ticks` | axis labels from the top (max) down to 0, evenly spaced |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.forecast` `.forecast-axis` `.forecast-bar` `.forecast-current` `.forecast-delta` `.forecast-fill` `.forecast-floor` `.forecast-held` `.forecast-label` `.forecast-label-low` `.forecast-label-now` `.forecast-low` `.forecast-low-text` `.forecast-tick` `.forecast-up`

```lua
local forecast_chart = use "forecast-chart"

forecast_chart { bars = { { current = true, delta = "$46.8M", label = "Today", low = false, value = 46.8 }, { current = false, delta = "−2.8", label = "Nov 2", low = false, value = 44 }, { current = false, delta = "+9.2", label = "Nov 9", low = false, value = 53.2 }, { current = false, delta = "−16.8", label = "Nov 16", low = false, value = 36.4 }, { current = false, delta = "−15.3", label = "Nov 23", low = true, value = 21.1 }, { current = false, delta = "+11.9", label = "Nov 30", low = false, value = 33 } }, floor = 15, height = 160, max = 60, ticks = { "$60M", "$30M", "$0" } }
```

#### `guide-card`

**Guide Card.** A guide, article or course in a grid: a pastel band with an icon, the category in colour, the title, the read time, and progress, Done or New.

For one featured course with actions use `course-card`; for a plain titled box use `card`; for a linked record inside a message use `record-card`.

#### `heat-grid`

**Heat Grid.** A contribution grid of rounded squares: columns filled from the bottom by a count, or shaded cell by cell by level, with labels under the ends.

**When:** Activity over days or weeks at a glance: lessons per week, posts per day, a streak, a course's progress as squares, a GitHub-style contribution graph. For a count compared with the period before use `dot-chart`; for stacked counts with an axis use `bar-chart`; for one fraction use `meter` or `progress`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | the filled colour (default accent) |
| `columns` | list, left to right; each a count (squares filled from the bottom) or a list of levels from the top (0 empty, 1 to `levels` lighter to full) |
| `empty` | an empty square's colour (default muted-foreground at 10%) |
| `gap` | pixels between squares (default 4) |
| `labels` | texts under the grid, spread from the first column to the last |
| `levels` | shades for level lists (default 4); counts use the full colour |
| `rows` | squares per column (default: the tallest column) |
| `size` | a square's side in pixels (default 13) |
| `spread` | columns spread across the parent's width, the first and last at its edges |
| `tooltips` | one text per column, shown under the pointer |

**Styles:** `.heat-grid` `.heat-grid-cell` `.heat-grid-label`

```lua
local heat_grid = use "heat-grid"

-- Counts, filled from the bottom:
heat_grid { rows = 3, columns = { 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 1, 1, 1 },
	spread = true, size = 16, labels = { "Oct 5", "This week" } }
-- Levels, cell by cell (a single row of eight, two shades):
heat_grid { levels = 2, columns = { { 2 }, { 2 }, { 2 }, { 1 }, { 0 }, { 0 }, { 0 }, { 0 } } }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/heat-grid.luau`.

#### `kbd`

**Kbd.** Key caps for a shortcut, from a list of keys or a string like "cmd-shift-p" drawn with macOS glyphs.

**When:** Show a keyboard shortcut: in a menu row, a palette result, a tooltip line or a help sheet. Inside menus `menu` already draws one from an item's `shortcut`; for a word-like tag use `ui.badge`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `keys` | list of key labels ({ "⌘", "⇧", "P" }), or a string "cmd-shift-p"; spaces separate chords ("cmd-k cmd-s"). Names map to macOS glyphs: cmd/secondary ⌘, shift ⇧, alt/option ⌥, ctrl ⌃, enter ↩, tab ⇥, backspace ⌫, delete ⌦, arrows ↑↓←→, escape esc; single letters are upper-cased |
| `plain` | glyphs only, no cap borders (as in a macOS menu) |
| `small` | smaller caps, for menu rows |

**Styles:** `.kbd` `.kbd-chord` `.kbd-key` `.kbd-plain` `.kbd-small`

```lua
local kbd = use "kbd"

kbd { keys = "cmd-shift-p" }          -- ⌘ ⇧ P
kbd { keys = { "⌘", "K" } }
kbd { keys = "cmd-k cmd-s", small = true }
kbd { keys = "ctrl-tab", plain = true }
```

**KPI Cell.** A key figure in a dashboard's top row: an icon tile and title with a menu, the value large with its change in a pill, and a caption.

#### `kpi-meter`

**KPI Meter.** A headline figure with a dot and title, the value beside a caption, a bar of rounded segments and a mono legend.

**When:** A strip of headline figures where each one is a part of a whole (on time / late, fixed / open, one segment per notice). For a figure with a change pill use `kpi-cell`; for one fraction use `meter`; for a whole split into labelled parts in a card use `share-bar`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `caption` | muted text beside the figure |
| `caption_color` | a colour for the caption instead of muted ("danger") |
| `dot` | colour of the dot before the title (default accent) |
| `legend` | list of { text, color? }: dotted mono labels under the bar, spread across it |
| `mono` | set the figure in the monospace font |
| `msg` | message the ↗ sends; no arrow without it |
| `segments` | list of { share (any unit, summed), color?, dot? (a small round end marker), label? (tooltip) }, left to right |
| `title` | what it counts |
| `to` | mod to send `msg` to, if not the drawing one |
| `value` | the figure, as text |
| `width` | the bar's width in pixels (default 190) |

**Styles:** `.kpi-meter` `.kpi-meter-arrow` `.kpi-meter-arrow:hover` `.kpi-meter-bar` `.kpi-meter-caption` `.kpi-meter-dot` `.kpi-meter-legend` `.kpi-meter-mono` `.kpi-meter-segment` `.kpi-meter-title` `.kpi-meter-value`

```lua
local kpi_meter = use "kpi-meter"

kpi_meter { caption = "of 55 invoices left", dot = "#c9961a", legend = { { color = "#6f9bd1", text = "46 fixed" }, { color = "#c9961a", text = "9 open" } }, msg = "open", segments = { { color = "#6f9bd1", share = 46 }, { color = "#c9961a", share = 9 } }, title = "Exceptions open", value = "9" }
```

#### `line-chart`

**Line Chart.** Solid and dashed lines over periods with faint columns behind, an axis, labels, and a picked period with a rule, dots and a floating card.

**When:** A measure over days or weeks compared with a forecast or a target (actual against predicted, this year against last), where the user picks a day to read its figures. For several readings on one scale with a legend and a crosshair use `series-chart`; for bars against a floor use `forecast-chart`; for stacked counts use `bar-chart`; for a bare trend use `ui.line` or `sparkline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bars` | faint columns behind the lines, one value per period |
| `card` | element floating beside the picked period (its figures) |
| `card_width` | the card's width in pixels, to keep it inside the plot (default 170) |
| `event` | key of the message a period sends, default "point": { point = index } |
| `height` | the plot's height in pixels (default 180) |
| `labels` | one label per period, under the plot |
| `max` | the value at the top of the plot |
| `min` | the value at the bottom (default 0) |
| `selected` | index of the picked period: a rule, dots, and `card` |
| `series` | list of { name?, points (one per period), color? (default accent), dashed? }; the first is drawn under the next |
| `ticks` | axis labels from the top (max) down to the bottom, evenly spaced |
| `tips` | tooltip text per period, shown under the pointer |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | the plot's width in pixels (default 600) |

**Styles:** `.line-chart` `.line-chart-bar` `.line-chart-base` `.line-chart-card` `.line-chart-label` `.line-chart-label-on` `.line-chart-marker` `.line-chart-point` `.line-chart-rule` `.line-chart-slot` `.line-chart-slot:hover` `.line-chart-tick`

```lua
local line_chart = use "line-chart"

line_chart { bars = { 6, 5, 6, 7, 6, 6, 6, 5 }, height = 160, labels = { "21 Oct", "22 Oct", "23 Oct", "24 Oct", "25 Oct", "26 Oct", "27 Oct", "28 Oct" }, max = 15, selected = 4, series = { { color = "#3f9a5c", dashed = true, name = "Predicted", points = { 6, 4, 6, 7, 5, 3, 5, 4 } }, { color = "#3f73b5", dashed = false, name = "Actual", points = { 3, 6, 11, 9, 8, 9, 9, 3 } } }, ticks = { "15", "10", "5", "0" }, width = 520 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/line-chart.luau`.

#### `meter`

**Meter.** A bar filled to a fraction from 0 to 1, with the percentage beside it; it warns past a threshold.

**When:** A fraction (0 to 1) as a bar with its percentage: memory, quota, progress of a known size. For work with no known size use `progress` with `busy`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | text before the bar |
| `value` | 0 to 1 |
| `warn` | fraction past which it shows the warning color |
| `width` | bar width in pixels |

```lua
local meter = use "meter"

meter { label = "Memory", value = 0.62, width = 48 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/meter.luau`.

#### `metric`

**Metric.** A label, a value set large (or very large), and a note under it in a tone.

**When:** Headline figures across the top of a dashboard card: cash today, the lowest week, a total. For a figure in its own tile with a trend use `stat-tile`; for a status bar reading use `stat`; for a fraction use `meter`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | what it is |
| `note` | a line under it |
| `size` | "normal" (default) or "hero": the card's main figure |
| `tone` | the note's tone: success, danger, warning or muted (default) |
| `value` | the figure, as text |

**Styles:** `.metric` `.metric-hero` `.metric-label` `.metric-note` `.metric-value`

```lua
local metric = use "metric"

metric { label = "Lowest week", note = "Week of Jan 4", value = "$26.4M" }
```

#### `mini-bars`

**Mini Bars.** A few small labelled bars, one highlighted, future ones hatched: a figure by period at a glance.

**When:** A figure over a few periods in a KPI strip or a card header (revenue by month, signups by week). For a live trend in a status bar use `sparkline`; for a full chart with an axis use `bar-chart` or `forecast-chart`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bar` | each bar's width in pixels (default 18) |
| `bars` | list of { label, value, future? } |
| `height` | the tallest bar's height in pixels (default 40) |
| `highlight` | index of the bar to stand out (default the last that is not future) |

**Styles:** `.mini-bars` `.mini-bars-bar` `.mini-bars-future` `.mini-bars-label` `.mini-bars-on`

```lua
local mini_bars = use "mini-bars"

mini_bars { bars = { { future = false, label = "Jul", value = 18 }, { future = false, label = "Aug", value = 26 }, { future = false, label = "Sep", value = 21 }, { future = false, label = "Oct", value = 33 }, { future = false, label = "Nov", value = 41 }, { future = true, label = "Dec", value = 38 } } }
```

#### `note-card`

**Note Card.** A numbered review note: yellow numbered circle, file:line, text and a × remove button; selectable.

**When:** Notes a person leaves on lines while reviewing, to send to an agent; list them in a column beside a `diff-view`. For an authored comment use `comment-card`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | click message key instead of "select": sends { [event] = id } |
| `id` | the note's id, sent in messages (default its number) |
| `location` | file:line it points at |
| `number` | shown in the circle |
| `remove` | × message key instead of "remove": sends { [remove] = id } |
| `selected` | highlight it |
| `text` | the note |
| `to` | the mod to send them to |

**Styles:** `.note-card` `.note-card:hover` `.note-card:selected` `.note-card-location` `.note-card-number` `.note-card-number-text` `.note-card-remove` `.note-card-remove:hover` `.note-card-remove-icon` `.note-card-text`

#### `numbered-list`

**Numbered List.** Items in order, numbered in a muted column, wrapping text aligned.

**When:** Ordered steps or suggestions in a message, a note or a help page. For a checklist use `task-row`; for events in time use `timeline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `items` | the items' text |
| `start` | the first number (default 1) |

#### `pill`

**Pill.** A small tinted label with an optional icon, in a tone or any colour; clickable when given `msg`.

**When:** A tag on a row ("Work", "Health") or a count inside a sentence ("2 events"), where colour carries meaning. For several read-only labels use `tags`; for filters the user toggles use `chips`; for a plain status word use `ui.badge`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | any colour instead of a tone, such as "#3b82f6"; the tint is its 14% |
| `icon` | icon before the text |
| `label` | the text |
| `msg` | message a click sends |
| `size` | "small" (default, for tags) or "normal" (in a sentence) |
| `to` | mod to send `msg` to, if not the drawing one |
| `tone` | neutral (default), accent, success, warning or danger |
| `tooltip` | text under the pointer |

**Styles:** `.pill` `.pill-label` `.pill-normal`

```lua
local pill = use "pill"

pill { label = "Work", color = "#3b82f6" }
pill { label = "2 events", icon = "calendar", tone = "danger", size = "normal", msg = "show-events" }
```

#### `pixel-icon`

**Pixel Icon.** A pixel-art sprite on a rounded tile, from a grid of digits and a palette; mirrored to make a symmetric face.

**When:** A playful, recognisable mark for an agent, a bot, a project or a workspace, at any size from a list row (18 px) to a header (64 px). For a person's initial use `avatar`; for a generic glyph use `ui.icon`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `colors` | the tile's colour first, then one colour per digit |
| `mirror` | repeat each row reversed, so the pattern is the left half (default true) |
| `pattern` | rows of digits, top first: 0 is the tile, 1 to 9 are `colors[2]` to `colors[10]` (with `mirror`, only the left half) |
| `size` | the tile's side in pixels (default 40) |
| `tooltip` | text under the pointer |

**Styles:** `.pixel-icon`

```lua
local pixel_icon = use "pixel-icon"

pixel_icon { colors = { "#6fd3e6", "#f4f4f7", "#c9a7e8" }, pattern = { "0011", "0122", "0011", "0002", "0011", "0002", "0022", "0111" }, size = 48 }
```

#### `progress`

**Progress.** A thin rounded progress bar filled to a fraction, or a striped busy bar with a spinner, with an optional label and percentage.

**When:** Progress of a task: a download, an index, a build step. Use `busy = true` when the size is unknown. For a reading such as memory use `meter`; for a quota with a reset use `usage-bar`; for a spinner alone use `ui.icon { name = "loader-circle", spin = true }`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `busy` | unknown size: a striped track and a spinning loader |
| `detail` | text above the bar, right (default the percentage) |
| `height` | bar thickness in pixels (default 4) |
| `label` | text above the bar, left |
| `percent` | false hides the percentage |
| `tone` | accent (default) \| success \| warning \| danger \| muted |
| `value` | 0 to 1 |
| `width` | bar width in pixels (default 240) |

**Styles:** `.progress` `.progress-danger` `.progress-detail` `.progress-fill` `.progress-label` `.progress-muted` `.progress-spin` `.progress-stripe` `.progress-success` `.progress-track` `.progress-warning`

```lua
local progress = use "progress"

progress { detail = "1,284 of 2,006 files", label = "Indexing workspace", value = 0.64, width = 280 }
```

#### `progress-stack`

**Progress Stack.** A horizontal bar of stacked segments toward a target, solid or hatched, with a labelled marker and a ticked axis.

**When:** How far a goal is (a raise, a budget, a quota) split by stage: closed, out, soft, still needed, with where the pace leads. For one fraction use `meter`; for a quota with a reset use `usage-bar`; for task progress use `progress`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `labels` | axis labels, evenly spaced from the left end to the right |
| `marker` | { value, label }: a line and a pill over the bar ("Pace $69M") |
| `segments` | list of { value, color? or tone? (default accent), hatch? }, left to right |
| `ticks` | small ticks along the axis (default 40) |
| `total` | the value at the right end (the target) |
| `width` | pixels (default 520) |

**Styles:** `.progress-stack` `.progress-stack-bar` `.progress-stack-label` `.progress-stack-marker` `.progress-stack-pill` `.progress-stack-pill-text` `.progress-stack-segment` `.progress-stack-tick`

```lua
local progress_stack = use "progress-stack"

progress_stack { labels = { "$0M", "$25M", "$50M", "Target $75M" }, marker = { label = "Pace $69M", value = 69 }, segments = { { color = "accent", hatch = false, value = 41.3 }, { color = "accent/45", hatch = false, value = 8.5 }, { color = "accent/60", hatch = true, value = 12 }, { color = "danger", hatch = true, value = 13.2 } }, total = 75, width = 420 }
```

**Record Card.** A compact card for a linked record: a bold title, then an icon and a muted line saying what it is.

| `detail` | what it is, muted ("Deal · Negotiation · $98,000") |
| `icon` | icon before the detail |
| `msg` | message a click sends |
| `title` | the record's name |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |

#### `relative-time`

**Relative Time.** Elapsed seconds as "just now", "5 min ago", "yesterday", "3 days ago", or compact "5m", "2h", "3d".

**When:** An age or last-updated time in rows, cards and headers. Pass elapsed `seconds`: the mod computes them from a provider's timestamp and the current time. Use `compact` in tight columns (PR lists, tables). For a dated list of events use `timeline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `compact` | "5m", "2h", "3d", "4w", "1y" instead of words |
| `prefix` | words before it, e.g. "updated" |
| `seconds` | seconds elapsed (the mod computes them from a provider's timestamp) |
| `size` | text size (default small) |
| `tooltip` | text under the pointer, e.g. the exact date |

**Styles:** `.relative-time`

```lua
local relative_time = use "relative-time"

relative_time { prefix = "updated", seconds = 266400, tooltip = "2026-10-28 14:02" }
```

#### `rich-text`

**Rich Text.** A line of runs: plain, bold, muted or mono words and small outlined tag pills, side by side; a run can be clickable.

**When:** A sentence that mixes emphasis and labels in one line: an audit log's activity, a notification, a table cell ("Order #1213 marked as [Fulfilled]"). For a paragraph use `ui.text`; for a lone label use `pill` or `ui.badge`; for several labels use `tags`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `parts` | list of strings (plain) or { text, strong?, muted?, mono?, icon?, msg? } or { tag = "Fulfilled", tone? (accent, success, warning, danger) } |
| `size` | text size: small or normal (default) |
| `to` | mod to send a run's `msg` to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.rich-text` `.rich-text-link:hover` `.rich-text-mono` `.rich-text-muted` `.rich-text-strong` `.rich-text-tag` `.rich-text-tag-accent` `.rich-text-tag-danger` `.rich-text-tag-success` `.rich-text-tag-text` `.rich-text-tag-warning`

```lua

	{ text = "Product \"Harbor Hoodie\"", strong = true },

} }
```

#### `series-chart`

**Series Chart.** Lines for several series over a value and a time axis, with a legend, a hover hairline with values, and a pinned dashed crosshair with a card.

**When:** Several readings over the same period compared on one scale (CPU, GPU and memory over 24 hours; requests and errors by hour), where the reader wants a sample's exact values. For counts stacked per bucket use `bar-chart`; for periods against a forecast with a picked day's card use `line-chart`; for one small trend use `ui.line` or `sparkline`; for a balance against a floor use `forecast-chart`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | key of the message a click on the plot sends, default "pin": { pin = index } |
| `height` | the plot's height in pixels (default 180) |
| `labels` | time-axis labels: { index (the sample, from 1), text } |
| `legend` | false hides the legend |
| `max` | the value at the top (default 100) |
| `min` | the value at the bottom (default 0) |
| `pinned` | the sample the crosshair is pinned to; none when unset |
| `series` | list of { name, color, points }: the same number of points in each, oldest first |
| `ticks` | value-axis labels from the top down, one grid line each (default 100%, 75%, 50%, 25%, 0%) |
| `titles` | a heading per sample for the tooltip and the card ("TODAY, 06:00") |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |
| `unit` | after each value (default "%") |
| `width` | the plot's width in pixels (default 640); the axis adds 50 |

**Styles:** `.series-chart` `.series-chart-cross` `.series-chart-dash` `.series-chart-dot` `.series-chart-grid` `.series-chart-hit` `.series-chart-hit:hover` `.series-chart-key` `.series-chart-legend` `.series-chart-tick` `.series-chart-tip` `.series-chart-tip-row` `.series-chart-tip-title`

```lua
local series_chart = use "series-chart"

series_chart {
	width = 640, height = 180, pinned = state.pinned, titles = app.metrics.times,
	series = {
		{ name = "CPU", color = "#3b82f6", points = history.cpu },
		{ name = "GPU", color = "#22c55e", points = history.gpu },
	},
	labels = { { index = 1, text = "12:00" }, { index = 97, text = "NOW" } },
}
-- update: msg.pin is the clicked sample's index; keep it in state.pinned
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/series-chart.luau`.

**Share Bar.** A horizontal bar split into coloured shares with small gaps, each as wide as its share of the whole.

#### `sparkline`

**Sparkline.** Recent samples (0 to 1) as tiny bars, newest on the right, in a fixed width; samples past `hot` turn to the warning color.

**When:** Recent samples as tiny bars, like CPU over the last minute, in a status bar or header.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `height` | pixels |
| `hot` | value past which a bar turns warning |
| `samples` | how many bars to show |
| `values` | samples from 0 to 1, oldest first |

**Spotlight Bars.** Tall rounded columns sharing the width, one in the spotlight with a gradient and a lit label; a click moves it.

| Prop | Meaning |

| `bar` | each bar's width in pixels; unset, bars share the width |

#### `spreadsheet`

**Spreadsheet.** A spreadsheet grid: row numbers, typed column headers, grid lines, a highlighted row, an outlined cell with a caret, skeleton cells and empty rows.

**When:** Data laid out as a spreadsheet the user (or an agent) fills cell by cell: research sheets, imports, editable records, with cells still loading shown as skeleton bars. For a read-only list of records with sorting use `table`; for label/value pairs use `key-values`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `blank` | empty numbered rows after the data (default 0) |
| `caret` | draw a caret after the selected cell's content (someone is typing) |
| `columns` | list of { key, title, icon? or glyph? (a short text such as "%" or "$") before the title, width (px; else it grows), align (left\|center\|right), skeleton? (bar width, px) } |
| `current` | index of the highlighted row (the one being worked on) |
| `event` | key of the message a cell click sends, default "cell": { cell = { row, key } } |
| `grow` | fill the parent and scroll the rows |
| `height` | pixels: the rows scroll within it |
| `numbers` | false hides the row number column |
| `row_height` | pixels per row (default 34) |
| `rows` | list of maps, a value per column key: text, a number, an element, `false` for a skeleton bar, or nil for empty |
| `selected` | { row, key }: the outlined cell |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.spreadsheet-caret` `.spreadsheet-cell` `.spreadsheet-cell-selected` `.spreadsheet-grid` `.spreadsheet-head` `.spreadsheet-head-cell` `.spreadsheet-head-icon` `.spreadsheet-head-text` `.spreadsheet-number` `.spreadsheet-number-text` `.spreadsheet-row` `.spreadsheet-row:hover` `.spreadsheet-row:selected` `.spreadsheet-skeleton` `.spreadsheet-text`

```lua
local spreadsheet = use "spreadsheet"

spreadsheet {
	columns = {
		{ key = "company", title = "Company", icon = "case-sensitive", width = 150 },
		{ key = "apy", title = "APY", glyph = "%", width = 80 },
		{ key = "fee", title = "Monthly fee", glyph = "$", width = 100 },
		{ key = "source", title = "Source", icon = "link" },
	},
	rows = state.rows, -- { { company = "Bayline", apy = "4.35%", fee = false, source = "bayline.com" }, ... }
	current = 2, selected = { row = 2, key = "fee" }, caret = true,
	blank = 4, grow = true,
} -- sends { cell = { row = 2, key = "fee" } }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/spreadsheet.luau`.

#### `stat-tile`

**Stat Tile.** A dashboard tile: label, big value with unit, a delta with an up or down arrow in good or bad colour, a note, and optional content.

**When:** A headline number on a dashboard or overview: open PRs, tokens today, uptime, failing checks; put several in a wrapping row. For a status bar reading use `stat`; for a fraction use `meter`; for a quota use `usage-bar`; for a series use `bar-chart`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | anything under the value: a sparkline, a meter |
| `delta` | change, e.g. "+12%" or "−3" |
| `detail` | muted line under the value, e.g. "vs last week" |
| `good` | up (default) \| down: which direction is good, for the delta's colour |
| `icon` | an icon beside the label |
| `label` | what it counts |
| `msg` | message sent on a click |
| `selected` | highlight it (a chosen filter) |
| `to` | the mod to send `msg` to |
| `trend` | up \| down \| flat (default from the delta's sign) |
| `unit` | small text after the value ("ms", "%", "tokens") |
| `value` | the number, as text |
| `width` | pixels (default: as wide as its parent gives) |

**Styles:** `.stat-tile` `.stat-tile:hover` `.stat-tile:selected` `.stat-tile-bad` `.stat-tile-delta` `.stat-tile-delta-text` `.stat-tile-detail` `.stat-tile-flat` `.stat-tile-good` `.stat-tile-icon` `.stat-tile-label` `.stat-tile-unit` `.stat-tile-value`

```lua
local stat_tile = use "stat-tile"

stat_tile { delta = "+12%", detail = "vs. yesterday · 3 agents", icon = "activity", label = "Tokens today", value = "1.84M", width = 240 }
```

#### `table`

**Table.** Columns over selectable rows, with a sortable header showing the sort arrow, a column of checkboxes, rich cells, zebra stripes or a bordered card look, hover, and an empty text.

**When:** Tabular data with several aligned fields per row: devices, processes, files, runs; an admin list (audit log, orders) as `bordered` and `checkable`, with `filter-dropdown`s over it and `pagination` under it. For one field per row use `list`; for pull requests use `pr-row`; for label/value pairs use `key-values`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bordered` | frame it as a rounded card with a tinted header in sentence case and lines between rows |
| `check` | key of the message a row's box sends, default "check": { check = id } |
| `check_all` | message the header's box sends (default { check_all = true }); it shows checked when every row is, a dash when some are |
| `checkable` | a leading column of checkboxes, in the header too |
| `checks` | the checked rows' ids: a list, or a set { [id] = true } |
| `columns` | list of { key, title, width (px; else it grows), align (left\|center\|right), mono, muted, sortable } |
| `descending` | the sort arrow points down |
| `empty` | text shown when there are no rows (default "Nothing to show") |
| `event` | row message key instead of "select": sends { [event] = id } |
| `grow` | fill the parent and scroll the body |
| `height` | pixels: the body scrolls within it |
| `rows` | list of maps: `id` plus a value per column key; a value may be a string, a number or an element |
| `selected` | id of the selected row |
| `sort` | key of the sorted column (shows an arrow) |
| `sortable` | false makes no header clickable (a column can also set `sortable = false`) |
| `to` | the mod to send { sort = key } and { select = id } to |
| `zebra` | stripe every other row |

**Styles:** `.table` `.table-bordered` `.table-cell` `.table-cell-bordered` `.table-cell-mono` `.table-cell-muted` `.table-check` `.table-check:hover` `.table-check:selected` `.table-empty` `.table-empty-text` `.table-header` `.table-header-bordered` `.table-heading` `.table-heading:hover` `.table-heading-sorted` `.table-heading-text` `.table-heading-text-bordered` `.table-row` `.table-row:hover` `.table-row:selected` `.table-row-bordered` `.table-row-last` `.table-row-odd`

```lua
local table_view = use "table"

table_view {
	columns = {
		{ key = "name", title = "Device" },
		{ key = "cpu", title = "CPU", width = 56, align = "right", mono = true },
		{ key = "seen", title = "Seen", width = 56, align = "right", muted = true },
	},
	rows = state.devices, -- { { id = "studio", name = "mac-studio", cpu = "42%", seen = "now" }, ... }
	selected = state.selected, sort = state.sort, descending = state.descending,
	zebra = true, grow = true,
} -- sends { sort = key } and { select = id }

-- An admin table: a card frame, a box per row, rich cells.
table_view {
	bordered = true, checkable = true, checks = state.checks, -- { [id] = true }
	check_all = { check_all = page_ids }, -- the ids on show, to tick them all
	columns = { { key = "activity", title = "Activity" }, { key = "time", title = "Timestamp", width = 220 } },
	rows = { { id = "a1", activity = rich_text { parts = parts }, time = "10/30/2026 09:12 AM" } },
} -- a box sends { check = id }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/table.luau`.

#### `tags`

**Tags.** Badges in a row that wraps, for labels, states or names.

**When:** A wrapping set of small labels: languages, topics, states.

| Prop | Meaning |

| `tags` | list of strings |
| `tone` | badge tone |

```lua
local tags = use "tags"

tags { tags = { "rust", "gpui", "luau", "wasm" } }
```

#### `threshold-line`

**Threshold Line.** A trend line with a dashed threshold labelled in a chip, breaching stretches in red, and a dot on the latest value.

**When:** A metric against its target or limit in a dashboard card: % within SLA against 95%, latency against 2s, lag against 5 minutes. For a line without a target use `ui.line`; for tiny bars use `sparkline`; for bars against a floor use `forecast-chart`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `breach` | "above" or "below": which side of the threshold is bad; those stretches turn danger (default none) |
| `dot` | false hides the dot on the latest value |
| `height` | pixels (default 56) |
| `label` | the chip at the threshold's right end ("95%", "2S"); no chip without it |
| `max` | the value at the top (default the highest point or threshold, with room) |
| `min` | the value at the bottom (default the lowest point or threshold, with room) |
| `points` | the values, oldest first, evenly spaced |
| `stroke` | line width in pixels (default 1.5) |
| `threshold` | the target or limit, drawn across dashed |
| `tooltip` | text under the pointer |
| `width` | pixels, chip included (default 220) |

**Styles:** `.threshold-line-breach` `.threshold-line-chip` `.threshold-line-chip-text` `.threshold-line-dot` `.threshold-line-dot-breach` `.threshold-line-stroke`

```lua
local threshold_line = use "threshold-line"

threshold_line { breach = "below", height = 64, label = "95%", points = { 97.2, 96.9, 95.8, 95.7, 95.6, 96.4, 96.2, 96.6, 97.4 }, threshold = 95, width = 320 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/threshold-line.luau`.

#### `tick-meter`

**Tick Meter.** A utilization bar made of thin vertical ticks, filled in a colour up to the value and dim after it.

**When:** A resource's utilization in a dense, technical dashboard (CPU, GPU, memory, a queue's depth), where a striped instrument reads better than a smooth bar. For a compact bar with its percentage use `meter`; for a quota with a reset use `usage-bar`; for task progress use `progress`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | the lit ticks' colour (default accent) |
| `height` | pixels (default 26) |
| `ticks` | how many ticks across (default 110) |
| `tooltip` | text under the pointer (default the percentage) |
| `value` | 0 to 1: the share of ticks lit |

**Styles:** `.tick-meter` `.tick-meter-on` `.tick-meter-tick`

```lua
local tick_meter = use "tick-meter"

tick_meter { color = "#3b82f6", value = 0.57 }
```

#### `timeline`

**Timeline.** A vertical rail of dots with one entry per line (time, mono title, detail, diff counts) and day headings; entries are selectable.

**When:** Events in order: checkpoints, commits, deploys, an agent's steps. For a flat selectable list use `list`; for comments use `comment-card`; for a table of runs use `table`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `empty` | text when there are no entries |
| `entries` | list of { id, day (a heading shown when it changes), time, title, detail, added, removed, tone (accent\|success\|warning\|danger\|muted dot), icon (instead of the dot), msg } |
| `event` | message key instead of "select": sends { [event] = id } |
| `mono` | false sets titles in the sans font |
| `selected` | id of the selected entry |
| `to` | the mod to send it to |

**Styles:** `.timeline` `.timeline-body` `.timeline-day` `.timeline-day-text` `.timeline-detail` `.timeline-dot` `.timeline-dot-accent` `.timeline-dot-danger` `.timeline-dot-success` `.timeline-dot-warning` `.timeline-empty` `.timeline-entry` `.timeline-entry:hover` `.timeline-entry:selected` `.timeline-icon` `.timeline-line` `.timeline-rail` `.timeline-time` `.timeline-title` `.timeline-title-mono`

```lua
			{ id = "c2", day = "Yesterday", time = "18:20", title = "checkpoint-2",
```

#### `usage-bar`

**Usage Bar.** A quota limit: title and "97% left", reset time, a bar of what is left with a pace marker, and a note; its tone follows what is left.

**When:** A rate limit or quota with a reset (an AI plan's weekly or 5-hour window, an API budget), in a usage sheet or settings page. For a plain fraction use `meter`; for task progress use `progress`; for a single big number use `stat-tile`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `danger` | left fraction under which it turns danger (default 0.1) |

| `title` | the window's name, e.g. "Weekly" |
| `warn` | left fraction under which it turns warning (default 0.25) |
| `width` | bar width in pixels (default 300) |

**Styles:** `.usage-bar` `.usage-bar-fill` `.usage-bar-fill-danger` `.usage-bar-fill-warning` `.usage-bar-note` `.usage-bar-pace` `.usage-bar-resets` `.usage-bar-title` `.usage-bar-track`

#### `week-calendar`

**Week Calendar.** A calendar card: the month, Today and arrows, Day / Week / Month, then hours with events spanning them, or a month with event chips.

**When:** Meetings, bookings or shifts placed in time: a day or week of hours where events span their length and overlapping ones share the column, or a month of them. For picking a day without events use `month-grid` or `day-strip`; for events in order without hours use `timeline`; for a day's list use `task-row`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `column_width` | pixels per day in the week (default 184); the grid scrolls sideways past its width |
| `day_width` | pixels for the one column of the day view (default 560) |
| `days` | day and week: the columns, { id, label ("Sun 11"), today? } |
| `event` | key of an event's message, default "select": { select = id } |
| `events` | list of { id, day (a day id), start, finish (hours, 9.5 = 9:30), title, caption?, time? (text), mark? ("video", "meet", "chat", "call", "grid", an icon name, or an element), tooltip? } |
| `grow` | fill the parent (default true) |
| `gutter` | pixels for the hours' labels (default 64) |
| `header` | false hides the header |
| `height` | pixels instead of growing |
| `hour_height` | pixels per hour (default 96) |
| `hours` | { from = 8, to = 18 }: the hours shown |
| `more` | month: chips per day before "+N more" (default 3) |
| `next` | message the forward arrows send |
| `now` | { day, hour }: a line across that day at that hour |
| `pick_day` | key of a day's message, default "day": { day = id } |
| `previous` | message the back arrows send |
| `selected` | id of the chosen event |
| `switch` | key of the switch's message, default "view": { view = id } |
| `title` | header title ("January 2026"); the header shows with a title or arrows |
| `to` | mod to send them to, if not the drawing one |
| `today` | message the Today button sends; no button without it |
| `view` | "day", "week" (default) or "month" |
| `views` | the switch's options: ids from day, week, month (default all three); false hides it |
| `weekdays` | month: the heading's names (default Sun … Sat) |
| `weeks` | month: weeks of 7 { id, day ("11"), today?, outside? } |

**Styles:** `.week-calendar` `.week-calendar-arrow` `.week-calendar-arrow:hover` `.week-calendar-arrows` `.week-calendar-cell` `.week-calendar-cell:hover` `.week-calendar-cell-first` `.week-calendar-cell-number` `.week-calendar-cell-today` `.week-calendar-chip` `.week-calendar-chip:hover` `.week-calendar-chip:selected` `.week-calendar-chip-text` `.week-calendar-event` `.week-calendar-event:hover` `.week-calendar-event:selected` `.week-calendar-event-caption` `.week-calendar-event-head` `.week-calendar-event-time` `.week-calendar-event-title` `.week-calendar-grid` `.week-calendar-grip` `.week-calendar-head` `.week-calendar-head:hover` `.week-calendar-head-text` `.week-calendar-heads` `.week-calendar-hour` `.week-calendar-hour-label` `.week-calendar-hour-text` `.week-calendar-mark` `.week-calendar-mark-call` `.week-calendar-mark-chat` `.week-calendar-mark-meet` `.week-calendar-mark-plain` `.week-calendar-mark-video` `.week-calendar-month` `.week-calendar-month-name` `.week-calendar-more` `.week-calendar-nav` `.week-calendar-now` `.week-calendar-now-dot` `.week-calendar-outside` `.week-calendar-title` `.week-calendar-today` `.week-calendar-today-button` `.week-calendar-today-button:hover` `.week-calendar-top` `.week-calendar-week`

```lua
	title = "November 2026", view = state.view, today = "today", previous = "previous", next = "next",
	days = { { id = "2026-11-02", label = "Mon 2" }, { id = "2026-11-03", label = "Tue 3", today = true } },
```

### Feedback

#### `banner`

**Banner.** A full-width coloured strip with an icon, text, an optional action and a close button; soft or solid, in a tone.

**When:** A message across the whole window or pane that stays until dealt with: the current worktree's branch, a failed provider, an update ready. For a transient message use a toast (`ui.overlay` at `bottom-end`); for a status inside a row use `status-dot` or `ui.badge`; for an empty pane use `empty-state`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | { label, msg, to? } for a button on the right, or an element |
| `detail` | muted text after it |
| `dismiss` | msg for a close button on the far right (omit for none) |
| `icon` | icon before the text |
| `mono` | set the text in the monospace font (branch names, paths) |
| `solid` | fill with the tone (a yellow branch strip) instead of a tint |
| `text` | the message |
| `to` | mod to send the action and dismiss msgs to, if not the drawing one |
| `tone` | accent (default), warning, success, danger or muted |

**Styles:** `.banner` `.banner-accent` `.banner-action` `.banner-action:hover` `.banner-close` `.banner-close:hover` `.banner-danger` `.banner-detail` `.banner-mono` `.banner-muted` `.banner-solid-accent` `.banner-solid-danger` `.banner-solid-muted` `.banner-solid-success` `.banner-solid-warning` `.banner-success` `.banner-text` `.banner-warning`

```lua
local banner = use "banner"

banner { text = app.git and app.git.branch or "main", icon = "git-branch", tone = "warning", solid = true, mono = true }
banner { text = "The git provider stopped", detail = "exit status 1", icon = "triangle-alert", tone = "danger",
	action = { label = "Restart", msg = "restart-git" }, dismiss = "hide-banner" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/banner.luau`.

#### `empty-state`

**Empty state.** A centered icon, title, message and optional button for a panel with nothing to show yet.

**When:** A list, panel or page with nothing to show yet, optionally with one action to fix that. For loading use `loading-row`; for failures use `notice`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | button label |
| `icon` | icon name |
| `message` | one line on why or what to do |
| `msg` | sent when the button is clicked |
| `title` | what is missing |

```lua
local empty_state = use "empty-state"

empty_state { action = "New worktree", icon = "inbox", message = "Create one to work on two branches at once.", msg = "new", title = "No worktrees" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/empty-state.luau`.

#### `error-state`

**Error state.** An inline or centred failure: icon, message, mono details and a Retry button.

**When:** In place of content that failed to load (a list, a pane, a provider's data). For an in-page warning that isn't a failed load use `notice`; for a lost daemon or SSH connection use `reconnecting`; for nothing to show use `empty-state`; for a transient failure use `toast`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `block` | centre it in the space it gets |
| `details` | the raw error, shown in mono in a box |
| `icon` | icon; default `circle-alert` |
| `message` | why, or what to do |
| `retry` | msg for the Retry button (hidden when unset) |
| `retry_label` | default "Retry" |
| `retrying` | show the retry as running |
| `secondary` | a second button { label, msg }, e.g. Open logs |
| `title` | what failed, e.g. "Couldn't load pull requests" |
| `to` | mod the buttons send to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.error-state` `.error-state-actions` `.error-state-block` `.error-state-block-icon` `.error-state-details` `.error-state-icon` `.error-state-message` `.error-state-text` `.error-state-title`

```lua
local error_state = use "error-state"

error_state { details = "HTTP 401 Unauthorized: Bad credentials (GET /repos/penso/moonframe/pulls)", message = "GitHub refused the request. Check the token in Settings › Integrations.", retry = "retry", secondary = { label = "Open settings", msg = "open-settings" }, title = "Couldn't load pull requests" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/error-state.luau`.

#### `insight-note`

**Insight Note.** A soft tinted box with a sparkle label and a finding, with an optional underlined action inside the sentence.

**When:** An assistant's finding beside the data it explains (under a chart, over a table, in a checklist card). For a warning that must be dealt with use `notice`; for a conversation use `chat-message`; for a transient message use `toast`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `after` | text after the link, ending the sentence |
| `icon` | icon before the label (default sparkles) |
| `label` | the small heading (default "AI insight") |
| `link` | underlined action text after `text`; it sends `msg` |
| `msg` | message the link sends |
| `text` | the finding |
| `to` | mod to send `msg` to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.insight-note` `.insight-note-label` `.insight-note-link` `.insight-note-link:hover` `.insight-note-rule` `.insight-note-text`

```lua
local insight_note = use "insight-note"

insight_note { after = "and review the 9 unclear disputes.", link = "read the dates from invoice scans", msg = "read-scans", text = "Exceptions are running 29% above forecast since the last ledger sync. Recommend:" }
```

#### `key-hints`

**Key hints.** A muted footer line of keyboard hints, such as ↑↓ choose · ↵ open · esc close.

**When:** Under a palette, picker, list or dialog to say which keys work there. For a full reference of shortcuts use `shortcuts`; for one shortcut beside a menu item or button use `kbd`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `caps` | bordered key caps instead of plain glyphs |
| `hints` | list of { keys = "up down" or "enter" or { "↑", "↓" }, label } |
| `justify` | `start` (default), `center`, `end` or `between` |
| `separator` | text between hints; default "·" |

**Styles:** `.key-hints` `.key-hints-hint` `.key-hints-keys` `.key-hints-label` `.key-hints-separator`

```lua
local key_hints = use "key-hints"

key_hints { hints = { { keys = "up down", label = "choose" }, { keys = "enter", label = "open" }, { keys = "cmd-enter", label = "open in new tab" }, { keys = "escape", label = "close" } } }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/key-hints.luau`.

#### `loading`

**Loading.** A spinner with text, inline or centred as a block, or skeleton bars standing in for content.

**When:** While data loads: inline beside a label, centred in an empty pane (`block`), or as `skeleton` bars where rows will appear. For known progress use `progress`; for a lost connection use `reconnecting`; for a failure use `error-state`; for nothing to show use `empty-state`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `block` | centre it in the space it gets, larger, instead of a small inline row |
| `count` | number of skeleton bars; default 3 |
| `detail` | a muted second line (block only) |
| `skeleton` | draw placeholder bars instead of a spinner |
| `text` | what is loading; default "Loading…" |
| `widths` | skeleton bar widths in pixels, cycled; default full width with a shorter last bar |

**Styles:** `.loading` `.loading-bar` `.loading-block` `.loading-block-icon` `.loading-block-text` `.loading-detail` `.loading-icon` `.loading-skeleton` `.loading-text`

```lua
local loading = use "loading"

loading { text = "Fetching pull requests…" }
loading { block = true, text = "Connecting to devbox", detail = "ssh penso@devbox.local" }
loading { skeleton = true, count = 4 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/loading.luau`.

#### `notice`

**Notice.** An inline tinted callout with a tone icon, title, text, an optional action and ×; long text can fold behind Show more.

**When:** A message that belongs in the page and stays until handled: a config error, an announcement, a permission problem. For transient notifications use `toast`/`toasts`; for a failed load with Retry use `error-state`; for an empty list use `empty-state`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | extra content under the text (a code line, a list) |
| `action` | a button: { label, msg, variant } |
| `dismiss` | msg for a × in the corner (none when unset) |
| `expanded` | show all of a foldable text |
| `foldable` | cut `text` to one line until `expanded`, with a Show more link |
| `icon` | icon instead of the tone's own |
| `id` | sent back in the default dismiss and toggle msgs |
| `text` | the message |
| `title` | bold first line |
| `to` | mod the buttons send to, if not the drawing one |
| `toggle` | msg sent by Show more / Show less; default `{ toggle = id }` |
| `tone` | `info` (default), `success`, `warning` or `danger` |

**Styles:** `.notice` `.notice-actions` `.notice-close` `.notice-close:hover` `.notice-content` `.notice-danger` `.notice-icon` `.notice-icon-danger` `.notice-icon-success` `.notice-icon-warning` `.notice-more` `.notice-more:hover` `.notice-success` `.notice-text` `.notice-title` `.notice-warning`

```lua
local notice = use "notice"

notice { action = { label = "Open config.toml", msg = "open-config" }, dismiss = "hide-config-notice", expanded = false, foldable = true, id = "config", text = "Line 14: unknown key `sidebar.density`; it is ignored. Line 31: `theme = \"nord-light\"` is not an installed theme, so the default theme is used until you fix it or install it.", title = "config.toml has 2 problems", tone = "warning" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/notice.luau`.

#### `reconnecting`

**Reconnecting.** A card over the dimmed window while a host reconnects: spinner, host, reason, next attempt and Reconnect now.

**When:** A whole window or pane depends on a connection that dropped (the daemon, an SSH host, a cloud machine) and must wait for it. For a failed load inside one pane use `error-state`; for a brief note that something reconnected use `toast`; for plain loading use `loading`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `dismiss` | msg for Escape and backdrop clicks; unset keeps it up until the mod closes it |
| `host` | the host's name, in the title |
| `icon` | an icon instead of the spinner |
| `open` | show it |
| `reason` | why it dropped (muted) |
| `retry` | msg for Reconnect now (hidden when unset) |
| `retry_label` | default "Reconnect now" |
| `secondary` | a second button { label, msg } |
| `status` | small line such as "Next attempt in 4s" |
| `title` | instead of "Reconnecting to <host>…" |
| `to` | mod the buttons send to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.reconnecting` `.reconnecting-actions` `.reconnecting-body` `.reconnecting-reason` `.reconnecting-spinner` `.reconnecting-status` `.reconnecting-title`

```lua
local reconnecting = use "reconnecting"

reconnecting { host = "devbox", open = true, reason = "The SSH connection closed: Connection reset by peer.", retry = "reconnect", secondary = { label = "Work offline", msg = "offline" }, status = "Next attempt in 4s · attempt 3" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/reconnecting.luau`.

#### `release-notes`

**Release notes.** One release: version and date header, highlight cards with optional media, an Also fixed list; collapsible for older releases.

**When:** A What's new page, an update panel or a changelog list (one per release, older ones `collapsed`). For the update offer itself use `update-pill`; for a first-run tour use `onboarding`; for a dated activity feed use `timeline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `badge` | a badge after the version ("Latest", "Beta") |
| `collapsed` | only the header and a count line |
| `date` | release date text |
| `fixes` | list of strings for the Also fixed bullets |
| `fixes_title` | default "Also fixed" |
| `highlights` | list of { title, detail, icon, media } cards; `media` is an element (a `ui.image`) |
| `id` | id for the default toggle msg |
| `name` | app name before the version; default none |
| `summary` | a muted line under the header |
| `to` | mod to send the toggle to, if not the drawing one |
| `toggle` | msg the header sends to expand or collapse; default `{ toggle = id or version }` when set to `true` |
| `version` | the version, e.g. "1.4.0" |

**Styles:** `.release-notes` `.release-notes-bullet` `.release-notes-card` `.release-notes-card-detail` `.release-notes-card-icon` `.release-notes-card-title` `.release-notes-chevron` `.release-notes-count` `.release-notes-date` `.release-notes-fix` `.release-notes-fixes` `.release-notes-fixes-title` `.release-notes-head` `.release-notes-head-clickable:hover` `.release-notes-highlights` `.release-notes-media` `.release-notes-summary` `.release-notes-version`

```lua
local release_notes = use "release-notes"

release_notes { badge = "Latest", date = "October 28, 2026", fixes = { "The sidebar no longer jumps when an agent finishes.", "Pasting into a terminal with bracketed paste keeps tabs.", "Toasts stack upward instead of over each other." }, highlights = { { detail = "Every option in one place, grouped by page, with search and per-host overrides marked Local.", icon = "settings", title = "A settings window" }, { detail = "When an SSH host drops, Moonframe retries with backoff and keeps your panes where they were.", icon = "wifi", title = "Automatic reconnect" } }, name = "Moonframe", summary = "Settings get a new home, and remote hosts reconnect on their own.", version = "1.4.0" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/release-notes.luau`.

#### `thinking`

**Thinking.** A quiet fold saying how long an agent thought, showing its reasoning when open.

**When:** Inside an agent's `chat-message`, before its answer. For a spinner while it is still thinking use `loading`; for a general fold use `collapsible`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | the text instead of "Thought for N seconds" |
| `msg` | message a click sends (the mod flips `open`) |
| `open` | show the reasoning |
| `seconds` | how long it thought |
| `text` | the reasoning shown when open |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.thinking` `.thinking-head` `.thinking-head:hover` `.thinking-text`

```lua
local thinking = use "thinking"

thinking { open = true, seconds = 6, text = "Three late deals have had no contact in ten days." }
```

#### `toast`

**Toast.** One notification card: level dot or icon, source label, title, one-line body, an action button and ×.

**When:** A single transient notification, usually inside `toasts`, which stacks them in a window corner. For a message that stays in the page use `notice`; for a blocking question use `confirm`; for an app update use `update-pill`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | a button under the body: { label, msg } |
| `body` | muted text under the title, cut to one line unless `full` |
| `dismiss` | msg sent by the ×; default `{ [event or "dismiss"] = id }`; `false` hides the × |
| `event` | key of the default dismiss msg |
| `full` | show the whole body, wrapped |
| `icon` | an icon instead of the level dot (`true` for the level's own icon) |
| `id` | sent back on dismiss: `{ dismiss = id }` |
| `level` | `info` (default), `success`, `warning` or `error`: the dot and border color |
| `source` | small muted label over the title: a host, a mod, "Local" |
| `title` | first line |
| `to` | mod the action and × send to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | pixels; default 340 |

**Styles:** `.toast` `.toast-action` `.toast-body` `.toast-close` `.toast-close:hover` `.toast-content` `.toast-dot` `.toast-dot-error` `.toast-dot-success` `.toast-dot-warning` `.toast-error` `.toast-icon` `.toast-icon-error` `.toast-icon-success` `.toast-icon-warning` `.toast-source` `.toast-title` `.toast-warning`

```lua
local toast = use "toast"

toast { action = { label = "Reconnect", msg = "reconnect" }, body = "The daemon socket directory must be owned by your user and not world-writable.", full = true, id = "git-permissions", level = "warning", source = "Local", title = "Local Git and PR details unavailable" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/toast.luau`.

#### `toasts`

**Toasts.** A stack of toast cards floating in a window corner; each × sends { dismiss = id }.

**When:** The app's notifications: keep a list in the mod's state, push to it, remove on `dismiss` (or after a timer). For one card inline use `toast`; for a persistent callout in a page use `notice`; for an update offer use `update-pill`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | key of the dismiss msg; default `dismiss` |
| `items` | list of { id, level, icon, source, title, body, full, action = { label, msg } } |
| `max` | most cards shown at once (the newest); default 4 |
| `place` | overlay corner: `bottom-end` (default), `bottom-start`, `top-end`, `top-start`, `top`, `bottom` |
| `to` | mod the × and actions send to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | card width in pixels; default 340 |

**Styles:** `.toasts` `.toasts-stack`

```lua
local toasts = use "toasts"

toasts { items = { { body = "feature/inspect at ~/code/app-inspect", id = 1, level = "success", source = "moonframe", title = "Worktree created" }, { action = { label = "Reconnect", msg = "reconnect" }, body = "The daemon socket directory must be owned by your user and not world-writable.", id = 2, level = "warning", source = "Local", title = "Local Git and PR details unavailable" }, { body = "cargo test failed in crates/moonframe-core", icon = true, id = 3, level = "error", source = "devbox", title = "Agent exited with code 1" } } }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/toasts.luau`.

#### `update-pill`

**Update pill.** A pill offering an app update: "Moonframe 1.4 is ready", an accent Restart button, a What changed link and a round ×.

**When:** Tell the user an update is downloaded and ready to install, without interrupting. For the changelog itself use `release-notes`; for other notifications use `toast`/`toasts`; for a lasting in-page message use `notice`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `dismiss` | msg for the round × (hidden when unset) |
| `downloading` | a spinner and "Downloading…" instead of Restart |
| `floating` | float it over the window in a corner instead of drawing it inline |
| `icon` | icon before the text; default `rocket` |
| `name` | app name; default "Moonframe" |
| `notes` | msg for the What changed link (hidden when unset) |
| `notes_label` | default "What changed" |
| `place` | corner when floating; default `bottom-end` |
| `restart` | msg for the Restart button; default `"restart"` |
| `restart_label` | default "Restart" |
| `text` | the whole message instead of "<name> <version> is ready" |
| `to` | mod the buttons send to, if not the drawing one |
| `version` | the new version |

**Styles:** `.update-pill` `.update-pill-close` `.update-pill-close:hover` `.update-pill-floating` `.update-pill-icon` `.update-pill-link` `.update-pill-link:hover` `.update-pill-restart` `.update-pill-text`

```lua
local update_pill = use "update-pill"

update_pill { dismiss = "later", name = "Moonframe", notes = "show-notes", version = "1.4" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/update-pill.luau`.

### Forms

#### `checkbox`

**Checkbox.** A box with a check mark (or a dash when indeterminate) and a label; a click sends `msg`.

**When:** An option that is on or off among others in a form or list, or a "select all" (indeterminate when some are). For a setting that applies at once use `switch`; for one of many use `radio-group`; for filter toggles use `chips`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `checked` | true when checked |
| `description` | muted line under the label |
| `disabled` | greys it out and ignores clicks |
| `indeterminate` | shows a dash: some but not all of a group are checked |
| `label` | text beside the box |
| `msg` | message a click sends (the mod flips its state) |
| `to` | mod to send `msg` to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.checkbox` `.checkbox:hover` `.checkbox-box` `.checkbox-box:selected` `.checkbox-box-top` `.checkbox-description` `.checkbox-disabled`

```lua
local checkbox = use "checkbox"

checkbox { label = "Restore tabs on launch", checked = state.restore, msg = "toggle-restore" }
checkbox { label = "All files", indeterminate = true, msg = "toggle-all" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/checkbox.luau`.

#### `choice-cards`

**Choice Cards.** A wrapping grid of selectable cards (preview, icon, title, description), the chosen one with an accent border and check; sends { select = id }.

**When:** Pick one of several options that are best seen: a theme, a layout, a template, an agent. For short text options use `segmented` or `radio-group`; for a colour use `swatches`; for a menu use `dropdown`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | key of the message a click sends, default "select": { select = id } |
| `options` | list of { id, title, description?, icon?, preview? (an element drawn on top), colors? (hex list drawn as a strip when there is no preview), disabled?, msg? } |
| `selected` | id of the chosen card |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | card width in pixels (default 180); the grid wraps |

**Styles:** `.choice-cards` `.choice-cards-card` `.choice-cards-card:hover` `.choice-cards-card:selected` `.choice-cards-check` `.choice-cards-color` `.choice-cards-description` `.choice-cards-disabled` `.choice-cards-icon` `.choice-cards-preview` `.choice-cards-title`

```lua
local choice_cards = use "choice-cards"

choice_cards {
	selected = state.layout,
	options = {
		{ id = "rounded", title = "Comfortable", icon = "layout-dashboard", description = "Roomy rounded rows" },
		{ id = "compact", title = "Compact", icon = "menu", description = "Dense rows, more fits" },
		-- preview = any element, drawn on top of the card:
		{ id = "dark", title = "Darkside", description = "Ghostty", colors = { "#222324", "#e8341c", "#68c256" } },
	},
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/choice-cards.luau`.

#### `composer`

**Composer.** A message box for an agent: a chip naming it, an attach button, the field and a round send button.

**When:** The bottom of a chat with an agent or a person. For a search box use `search-field`; for a longer form field use `ui.input` with `multiline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `agent` | who it goes to, in a chip above the field |
| `attach` | message the attach button sends; no button without it |
| `change` | sent on each edit, with `value` set to the text |
| `focus` | take focus when it appears |
| `icon` | the chip's icon (default sparkles) |
| `id` | keeps the text across renders (default "composer") |
| `placeholder` | grey text while empty |
| `send` | message the round button sends; a click cannot read the field, so the mod keeps the text from `change` |
| `submit` | sent on Enter and by the send button, with `value` |
| `to` | mod to send them to, if not the drawing one |
| `value` | the text; "" after sending clears it |

**Styles:** `.composer` `.composer-attach` `.composer-chip` `.composer-chip-icon` `.composer-field` `.composer-send`

```lua
local composer = use "composer"

composer { agent = "Sales agent", attach = "attach", placeholder = "Ask the sales agent anything…", send = "send", submit = "send" }
```

#### `radio-group`

**Radio Group.** Radio buttons, vertical or horizontal, each with a label and optional description; sends { select = id }.

**When:** Pick one of a few options that need a description or room to read (a mode, a policy). For 2 to 4 short values use `segmented`; for many values use `dropdown`; for options with a picture use `choice-cards`; for independent on/off options use `checkbox`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | key of the message a click sends, default "select": { select = id } |
| `horizontal` | lay the options out in a row |
| `options` | list of { id, label, description?, disabled?, msg? (sent instead of the default) } |
| `selected` | id of the chosen option |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.radio-group` `.radio-group-circle` `.radio-group-circle:selected` `.radio-group-description` `.radio-group-disabled` `.radio-group-dot` `.radio-group-horizontal` `.radio-group-option` `.radio-group-option:hover`

```lua
local radio_group = use "radio-group"

radio_group { options = { { description = "Each agent gets its own checkout and branch.", id = "worktree", label = "New worktree" }, { description = "Agents share the working tree you are in.", id = "current", label = "Current folder" }, { description = "Run on a remote box; needs a connected device.", disabled = true, id = "remote", label = "Cloud machine" } }, selected = "worktree" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/radio-group.luau`.

#### `search-field`

**Search field.** A one-line search box; edits send change with the text as `value`, Esc sends cancel, up and down move through results.

**When:** A query box over a list or palette: filter files, branches or commands as the user types, with up and down to move through results. For a longer value use `ui.input` (multiline for a text area); for one-of-many choices use `segmented` or `dropdown`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `cancel` | sent on Esc |
| `change` | sent on each edit, with `value` set to the text |
| `focus` | take focus when it appears |
| `id` | keeps the text across renders |
| `next` | sent on down |
| `placeholder` | grey text while empty |
| `previous` | sent on up |
| `submit` | sent on Enter |
| `to` | the mod the messages go to |
| `value` | the text; applied when it changes, so `""` clears it |
| `width` | pixels |

```lua
local search = use "search-field"

-- in view:
search {
	id = "files", value = state.query, placeholder = "Search files…",
	change = "query", cancel = "clear", previous = "up", next = "down",
}
-- in update: msg.msg == "query" sets state.query = msg.value;
-- "clear" sets state.query = "" (the field empties)
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/search-field.luau`.

#### `settings-row`

**Settings row.** A setting: title, source tag and muted description on the left, its control on the right, a line under it.

**When:** Each line of a settings page or preferences card, holding a `switch`, `segmented`, `dropdown` or button. Group rows under `settings-page` sections; for read-only properties use `key-values`; for a labelled switch on its own use `switch` with `label`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | the control(s) |
| `border` | the line under the row; default true |
| `description` | muted line under the title |
| `disabled` | grey the row out |
| `reason` | why it's disabled, shown under the description |
| `stacked` | put the control under the text (for wide controls such as a list of choices) |
| `tag` | a small chip after the title: where the value comes from ("Local", "Shared") |
| `tag_tone` | `local` (default, warning colour) or `shared` (muted) |
| `title` | the setting's name |

**Styles:** `.settings-row` `.settings-row-control` `.settings-row-description` `.settings-row-disabled` `.settings-row-flat` `.settings-row-head` `.settings-row-reason` `.settings-row-tag` `.settings-row-tag-shared` `.settings-row-text` `.settings-row-title`

```lua
local settings_row = use "settings-row"
local switch = use "switch"

settings_row { title = "Show agents", description = "List running agents under their workspace.",
	switch { on = state.show_agents, msg = "toggle-agents" },
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/settings-row.luau`.

#### `stepper`

**Stepper.** "− value +" in one bordered control, with an optional unit; the ends disable at min and max. Sends { step = -1 } and { step = 1 }.

**When:** A small number nudged up or down: a font size, a column count, a delay. For a fraction shown as a bar use `meter`; for one of a few named sizes use `segmented`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `decrement` | message − sends, default { step = -1 } |
| `increment` | message + sends, default { step = 1 } |
| `label` | text before the control |
| `max` | highest value; + is disabled there |
| `min` | lowest value; − is disabled there |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `unit` | text after the value ("px", "s") |
| `value` | the number shown |
| `width` | pixels for the value, wide enough for its longest reading (default 44) |

**Styles:** `.stepper` `.stepper-button` `.stepper-button:hover` `.stepper-button-disabled` `.stepper-group` `.stepper-label` `.stepper-separator` `.stepper-unit` `.stepper-value`

```lua
local stepper = use "stepper"

stepper { label = "Font size", max = 32, min = 8, unit = "px", value = 14 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/stepper.luau`.

#### `swatches`

**Swatches.** Colour swatches in a row with a ring on the chosen one and an optional "none"; a click sends { pick = color }.

**When:** Pick a colour from a short palette: a workspace or tag colour, an accent. For themes (many colours each) use `choice-cards` with a swatch row as the preview; to show colours without picking, use `ui.row`s with a background.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `colors` | list of hex strings ("#ef4444") or { color, label?, msg? } |
| `event` | key of the message a click sends, default "pick": { pick = color } |
| `none` | put a "none" swatch first; it sends { pick = "none" } |
| `selected` | the chosen colour, or "none" |
| `size` | swatch size in pixels (default 20) |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.swatches` `.swatches-none` `.swatches-ring` `.swatches-ring:hover` `.swatches-ring:selected` `.swatches-swatch`

```lua
local swatches = use "swatches"

swatches { colors = { "#ef4444", "#f97316", "#eab308", "#22c55e", "#14b8a6", "#3b82f6", "#8b5cf6", "#ec4899", "#64748b" }, none = true, selected = "#8b5cf6" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/swatches.luau`.

#### `switch`

**Switch.** An on/off switch (pill track and knob) with an optional label and description; a click sends `msg`.

**When:** A setting that takes effect at once, on or off ("High contrast"). For a choice that is confirmed later or part of a list of options use `checkbox`; for one of several values use `segmented` or `radio-group`.

| Prop | Meaning |

| `description` | muted line under the label |
| `disabled` | greys it out and ignores clicks |
| `label` | text beside the switch |
| `msg` | message a click sends (the mod flips its state) |

| `to` | mod to send `msg` to, if not the drawing one |

#### `task-check`

**Task Check.** A round check for a task: open, important (warning ring), in progress (danger ring with a dot), or done (filled with a check).

**When:** The check at the start of a task or to-do row; a click sends `msg` for the mod to flip it. For a form option use `checkbox`; for an agent's state use `status-dot`.

| `msg` | message a click sends |
